title: Morning Routine Expressive Visual Schedule
purpose: A visual schedule that shows morning routine order while preserving expressive options for waiting, help, change, finished and student comments.

teacherNotes.modeling: Point to schedule steps as they happen and model expressive messages, especially Wait, Help please, Change and Finished.
teacherNotes.evidence: Note whether the student anticipates next steps, requests help/wait/change, or comments on readiness.
teacherNotes.customisation: Replace routine steps with the actual class morning sequence and photos if available and approved.
teacherNotes.schedule_order: The first row and early second-row buttons are the routine sequence; the remaining buttons are expressive supports, not compliance controls.
teacherNotes.not_full_aac_claim: This is a visual schedule with communication supports. It is not a replacement for the student's full AAC system.

systemFit.existingSystem: Confirm how this support sits alongside the student's established AAC system.
systemFit.vocabularyAndMotorPlan: Confirm familiar vocabulary and stable locations before classroom use.
systemFit.symbolFamiliarity: Confirm that each symbol or text representation is recognised and meaningful.
systemFit.accessCalibration: Confirm access settings on the actual device with the student and team.
systemFit.positioningAndVision: Confirm screen, mounting, seating, visual field, contrast and fatigue conditions.
systemFit.languageCultureVoice: Confirm preferred language, culturally meaningful vocabulary and voice output.
systemFit.partnerSignals: Confirm reliable yes/no, cancel, repair and partner-assisted signals.

symbolStrategy.customMediaPolicy: teacher-owned local media only unless explicitly approved
symbolStrategy.notes: Routine search terms can be swapped for classroom photos where staff own the image and privacy is managed.

attribution.attribution: The pictographic symbols used are the property of the Government of Aragon and have been created by Sergio Palao for ARASAAC (https://arasaac.org), that distributes them under Creative Commons License BY-NC-SA.
attribution.note: Symbol search terms are provided for later ARASAAC replacement; confirm exact current licence wording when publishing beyond local classroom use.

sett.student: Student can understand the morning sequence and express wait, help, change, finished, or a question about what comes next.
sett.environment: Morning routine context with predictable order, real classroom photos if approved, and teacher modelling.
sett.task: Sequence the routine while preserving expressive communication and transition repair options.
sett.tools: Schedule-plus-expression grid, spoken labels, text fallback, stable repair buttons, and print-ready layout.

differentiation.content: Keep routine sequence visible while adding expressive agency.
differentiation.process: Model key vocabulary, provide wait time, allow rehearsal/repetition, and accept multimodal communication.
differentiation.product: Accept observed schedule use, expressive selection, print notes, or anonymous portfolio summary.
differentiation.environment: Use a calm, predictable, local-first layout with teacher controls separate from student choices.
differentiation.support: Teaching, SLP, OT, family, and student/team review should personalise vocabulary and access before reliance.

participationBarriers.barrier: Visual schedules can become receptive-only compliance tools.
participationBarriers.support: Add expressive options for wait, help, change, finished, and asking what comes next.

evidencePlan.notJudgement: Prompted routine use is participation/access evidence, not a standalone judgement of independence.
evidencePlan.export: Use anonymous teacher notes, print/portfolio evidence, or local CSV/report only when needed. Do not include diagnoses, behaviour details, family details, or school IDs.

provenance.sourcePrompt: Make a morning routine visual schedule with expressive options.
